Subject: Request: breakdown and expected credit after 2026-08-28 incident

Diego / Marissa,

Thanks again for the postmortem you shared yesterday. Our accounting team needs a concise breakdown of the service credit we should expect for the outage window on 2026-08-28 (approx 02:15–03:40 UTC). They also need the mechanism for issuance (credit memo vs invoice adjustment) and an estimated timeline.

Attached is our monitoring export (stratus_monitoring_export.csv) showing the spikes we observed. At a high level we are looking for:
- The exact downtime minutes you are counting as credit-eligible
- The formula used and the cap (if any)
- The dollar amount that will be applied to our next invoice or issued as a credit memo

Please let me know if you need more logs. We are hoping to have the accounting entry before our month-end close next week.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Stratus Analytics

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: breakdown and expected credit after 2026-08-28 incident

Alex — appreciate the clear ask and the attach. We've reviewed the event and here is the preliminary calculation and next steps.

Summary (pre-approval):
- Incident window considered: 2026-08-28 02:12:00 UTC — 2026-08-28 03:38:00 UTC (86 minutes).
- Eligible downtime after redundancy and maintenance exclusions applied: 72 minutes (we exclude 10 minutes of failover + 4 minutes maintenance window).

SLA and calculation used (per contract SOW section 3.2):
- Monthly uptime target = 99.95% (minutes in month = 43,200 for 30-day month).
- Downtime ratio = eligible_downtime_minutes / total_month_minutes = 72 / 43200 = 0.0016667 (~0.16667%).
- Service credit = min(downtime_ratio * monthly fee, 50% of monthly fee cap).

Applied to your committed Dedicated plan (monthly fee: $75,000):
- Downtime_ratio * monthly_fee = 0.0016667 * $75,000 = $125.00 (rounded).
- Cap (50%) = $37,500 — not reached.
- Preliminary credit amount = $125.00.

Notes and rationale:
- We do rounding to nearest dollar after the formula.
- Our legal/ops policy also allows for discretionary remediation credits for downstream impact; if you can show material business impact beyond the formula we can open a remediation review — that is not automatic and requires approvals.

Next steps I am requesting today:
1) Internal approval from finance for issuance as a credit memo (preferred by Stratus) or invoice adjustment.
2) If approved, we will issue the credit memo and send a DocuSign acknowledgement for your records.
3) Credit will appear on the next invoice cycle or can be applied immediately if billing confirms.

I have attached a short event summary (uptime-evt-summary.pdf) and the calculation worksheet. Marissa / Sean — can you confirm finance approval for the credit memo route and ETA for issuance?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(attachment: uptime-evt-summary.pdf)
